transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Ember CTO), Ethan Park (ML), Lila Nguyen (Prod) , Raj Singh (DevOps)

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Samir with Redwood, AE on the account, with Jules our solutions engineer. quick intro then we'll jump into your use case.
00:08 Maya: Hi Samir hi Jules, I'm Maya CTO at Ember, we build a customer support triage product, we use a mix of in-house ML and some third-party models.
00:15 Jules: great, could you say a bit about what you're trying to solve and what success looks like?
00:22 Maya: Sure — we want to add an assistant that classifies tickets, suggests responses, and does routing. main constraint is latency under 200ms for classification path, and cost needs to be reasonable. Also security; some PII in tickets so we need controls.
00:37 Ethan: and we want to evaluate hosted first, maybe Dedicated later if we hit production scale. also curious about on-prem private options for regulated customers.
00:46 Samir: perfect, that's exactly the flow most folks take — PLG quickstart with our hosted Redwood API to get to first token, then Dedicated or Private if you need VPC or on-prem.
00:56 Lila: what does quickstart actually look like? how long to get first token, what do you give us?
01:03 Jules: Good Q. For most teams it's minutes to first token. We have a self-serve sign up, free credits, SDKs and a Quickstart repo. we usually see engineers make a curl or SDK call inside the first hour; many in the first 10-30 minutes. We'll share the quickstart link and sample prompts.
01:20 Raj: does free credits require a card? any quota limits?
01:25 Samir: you can sign up with email and try credit — sometimes we require a card for larger trials to prevent abuse but small credits are cardless. quotas depend on plan; the console shows rate limits and you can request increases.
01:36 Ethan: from an infra POV, what telemetry and logs do we get? we need audit logs and ability to route logs into our SIEM.
01:44 Jules: hosted gives per-request metadata, logging, traces in Console. we support audit logs, and can forward via webhooks or integrations. For Dedicated/Private there are additional integrations like direct KMS and private network.
01:56 Maya: security: SOC2? SSO? KMS? data retention?
02:01 Samir: we are SOC2, we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, per-team keys, and customer-managed KMS for Private. retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted has default retention policies and options for extended retention as an add-on. we'll share the security pack.
02:19 Lila: any hidden gotchas on model parity between hosted and dedicated? we don't want drift in behavior when we move to Dedicated.
02:26 Jules: good point. we have version pinning and model catalog; same model families are available but sometimes different quantization or kernel choices on Dedicated. we provide verified performance profiles and recommended quantization profiles so you can get similar outputs.
02:42 Ethan: latency vs cost tradeoff — can you explain batching and KV caching; we need consistent p99s low.
02:50 Jules: Sure. We do smart routing, automatic batching and KV/prefix caching. For classification path you can use short-context optimized endpoints, maybe a smaller quantized model for cost. batching helps throughput but increases latency for low-volume single requests. We have a continuous-batching runtime that prioritizes latency-sensitive traffic. Also Dedicated gives predictable throughput so p99s are more stable.
03:12 Raj: for VPC/private do you offer a private control plane or fully air-gapped on-prem?
03:18 Samir: both options. Private has a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or an on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments — usually enterprise customers go that route.
03:26 Maya: what's involved in a pilot? we want to run a POC to validate latency and output quality, maybe 2-3 weeks.
03:32 Samir: typical pilot: 2-4 weeks, Redwood provides free credits, a dedicated channel to SE, and we run a small benchmark with your sample prompts. we'll help with eval prompts, instrumentation for latency/cost, and a roll out guide.
03:47 Lila: any examples of customers that started hosted then moved to Dedicated? curious about cost delta and lift.
03:53 Samir: yes — a fintech customer started hosted for quick iteration then committed to Dedicated once their throughput stabilized; they reduced unit cost by about 30% at scale and gained better p99s. we'll share an anonymized case study.
04:07 Ethan: curious about model catalog: can we bring our own models? fine-tune?
04:13 Jules: hosted supports fine-tuning for some families; Dedicated/Private supports bringing your own model artifacts and we can run quantization/compilation for the runtime. WYOD — bring your own model — is supported with enterprise onboarding.
04:25 Raj: do you have rate limiting that would throttle our pipeline? we will have bursts during business hours.
04:30 Samir: console lets you configure quotas and autoscaling policies for Dedicated; hosted has burst capacity and policies but if you need guaranteed throughput Dedicated is better. we can set up queueing/fallbacks to avoid hard failures.
04:45 Maya: on invoicing and pricing, is hosted pay-as-you-go? how does Reserved Dedicated pricing look?
04:51 Samir: hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embedding. Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commit; there are add-ons for observability retention or compliance. We'll send pricing tiers after the call.
05:05 Ethan: wanted to check developer experience — SDKs, examples for node/python, streaming, function calling?
05:11 Jules: Yes we have official SDKs for python/js (node), examples for streaming, function calling and structured output. Quickstart repo includes runnable examples.
05:21 Lila: do you support SSO provisioning and SCIM for user management?
05:25 Samir: yes SAML + SCIM supported for enterprise.
05:29 Maya: curious about how we measure quality regressions after model updates?
05:33 Jules: Console has evals and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts to test changes.
05:42 Ethan: one more on observability: token-level cost breakdown, trace correlation, per-route dashboards?
05:48 Jules: yep, per-route and per-model dashboards, traces, token-level cost, and exportable metrics.
05:54 Raj: for the quickstart, who will be our contact if we hit a blocker?
05:57 Samir: Jules will be your SE contact during the pilot, I'll be the AE for pricing and commercial.
06:03 Maya: timeline: we want to validate in two weeks and decide if Dedicated pilot is needed.
06:07 Samir: sounds good. we'll send the onboarding email with free credits, quickstart repo, and the benchmark sheet.
06:12 Lila: does Redwood support embedding-based reranking? we want to augment classification with embeddings for fuzzy match.
06:18 Jules: absolutely, embeddings API and reranking support are first-class. we have vector db integrations and you can call embeddings endpoint.
06:24 Ethan: curious about model latency numbers for small classification requests — do you have p50/p95 numbers for the curated models?
06:29 Jules: we'll share the verified performance profiles with p50/p95/p99 across hardware tiers — expect single-digit tens ms up to a few hundred ms depending on model and context length.
06:40 Maya: any legal/procurement concerns we should start preparing?
06:44 Samir: for enterprise purchases we do an initial SOW, standard enterprise agreement, and can provide SOC2 and other compliance docs. procurement sometimes asks about indemnities and DPA; we can work through that.
06:56 Lila: sounds good. can you include an example cURL to hit the quickstart endpoint?
06:59 Jules: yes I'll include that in the onboarding email.
07:05 Samir: quick recap: Samir send quickstart + pricing + security pack; Jules send benchmark spreadsheet and curl/examples; Ember team to sign up and validate time-to-first-token, run a few prompts, confirm latency and output quality within 2 weeks. Next meeting after pilot to review results.
07:21 Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate it.
07:24 Samir: thank you, we'll follow up.
